page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.8xlarge is a cloud server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs on a KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 256 GB of system RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Compute resources feature 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction set extensions including AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. Storage is provided via 7679 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD, complemented by a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps. This instance configuration does not include a GPU accelerator.

Performance profiles across synthetic and application benchmarks place the instance's multi-core execution in the average category, achieving a multi-core Geekbench score of 10415.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 27316.39. Multi-threaded decompression tasks achieve 130.48 GB/sec in bzip3 testing. In contrast, single-threaded performance lands in the lower quarter of cloud benchmarks, as indicated by a single-core stress-ng CPU score of 1318.1. Memory throughput testing records uncached large-block read speeds of 113.07 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 49.34 GB/sec. Database benchmark evaluations show a throughput of 28.0 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary strength of the ecs.i3.8xlarge lies in its substantial local SSD storage density paired with a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, offering qualitative cost efficiency for IOPS-sensitive and RAM-intensive deployments. A potential tradeoff involves lower single-threaded processing capability, making it less optimal for single-threaded processing bottlenecks. Appropriate workloads include high-throughput relational databases, distributed key-value caches like Redis, static web server clusters, and ETL data processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.8xlarge is a dedicated server instance equipped with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores at 2.5 GHz, 256 GB of RAM, and 7679 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Designed without a discrete GPU, it incorporates 10 Gbps baseline networking and hardware extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI. Multi-core compute performance and memory bandwidth test within average benchmark ranges, demonstrating 28.0 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 130.48 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, single-core CPU throughput sits in the lower performance tier. The instance's high local SSD capacity and 8.0 GB RAM per core deliver strong resource density for data-intensive applications. It is suited for high-throughput databases, key-value stores, static web serving, and ETL pipelines requiring attached local storage.
